# awscc_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint (Resource)

Resource Type definition for AWS::EC2::ClientVpnEndpoint



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `authentication_options` (Attributes List) Information about the authentication method to be used to authenticate clients. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--authentication_options))
- `connection_log_options` (Attributes) Information about the client connection logging options. If you enable client connection logging, data about client connections is sent to a Cloudwatch Logs log stream. The following information is logged: client connection requests, client connection results (successful and unsuccessful), reasons for unsuccessful client connection requests, client connection termination time. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--connection_log_options))
- `server_certificate_arn` (String) The ARN of the server certificate. For more information, see the AWS Certificate Manager User Guide.

### Optional

- `authorization_policy` (Attributes) The Cedar authorization policy to associate with the Client VPN endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--authorization_policy))
- `client_cidr_block` (String) The IPv4 address range, in CIDR notation, from which to assign client IP addresses. The address range cannot overlap with the local CIDR of the VPC in which the associated subnet is located, or the routes that you add manually. The address range cannot be changed after the Client VPN endpoint has been created. Client CIDR range must have a size of at least /22 and must not be greater than /12.
- `client_connect_options` (Attributes) The options for managing connection authorization for new client connections. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--client_connect_options))
- `client_login_banner_options` (Attributes) Options for enabling a customizable text banner that will be displayed on AWS provided clients when a VPN session is established. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--client_login_banner_options))
- `client_route_enforcement_options` (Attributes) Client route enforcement is a feature of the Client VPN service that helps enforce administrator defined routes on devices connected through the VPN. This feature helps improve your security posture by ensuring that network traffic originating from a connected client is not inadvertently sent outside the VPN tunnel.
Client route enforcement works by monitoring the route table of a connected device for routing policy changes to the VPN connection. If the feature detects any VPN routing policy modifications, it will automatically force an update to the route table, reverting it back to the expected route configurations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--client_route_enforcement_options))
- `description` (String) A brief description of the Client VPN endpoint.
- `device_posture_options` (Attributes) The device-posture trust providers to associate with the Client VPN endpoint. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--device_posture_options))
- `disconnect_on_session_timeout` (Boolean) Indicates whether the client VPN session is disconnected after the maximum sessionTimeoutHours is reached. If true, users are prompted to reconnect client VPN. If false, client VPN attempts to reconnect automatically.
- `dns_servers` (List of String) Information about the DNS servers to be used for DNS resolution. A Client VPN endpoint can have up to two DNS servers. If no DNS server is specified, the DNS address configured on the device is used for the DNS server.
- `endpoint_ip_address_type` (String) The IP address type of the Client VPN endpoint.
- `security_group_ids` (List of String) The IDs of one or more security groups to apply to the target network. You must also specify the ID of the VPC that contains the security groups.
- `self_service_portal` (String) Specify whether to enable the self-service portal for the Client VPN endpoint
- `session_timeout_hours` (Number) The maximum VPN session duration time in hours.
- `split_tunnel` (Boolean) Indicates whether split-tunnel is enabled on the AWS Client VPN endpoint.
- `tag_specifications` (Attributes List) The tags to apply to the Client VPN endpoint during creation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tag_specifications))
- `traffic_ip_address_type` (String) The IP address type of the Client VPN endpoint.
- `transit_gateway_configuration` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--transit_gateway_configuration))
- `transport_protocol` (String) The transport protocol to be used by the VPN session.
- `vpc_id` (String) The ID of the VPC to associate with the Client VPN endpoint. If no security group IDs are specified in the request, the default security group for the VPC is applied.
- `vpn_port` (Number) The port number to assign to the Client VPN endpoint for TCP and UDP traffic.

### Read-Only

- `client_vpn_endpoint_id` (String)
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.example
  identity = {
    id = "id"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String)

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform

  to = awscc_ec2_client_vpn_endpoint.example
  id = "id"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:
